documents: Wotzlaw et al. 2022, Sci. Adv. 8, eabk2184, published PDF (11 pages incl. cover sheet)

entry.evidence: However, the lifetime of the eruption-feeding magma chambers and the processes from magma chamber assembly to eruption remain poorly constrained.

sequences.source_document: Wotzlaw et al. 2022, Sci. Adv. 8, eabk2184 (published PDF)

steps.action: The authors pose the question of how long phonolitic magma chambers beneath Somma-Vesuvius are stored before eruption and how they evolve from assembly to eruption, noting that zircon and allanite are absent.
steps.quote: the lifetime of the eruption-feeding magma chambers and the processes from magma chamber assembly to eruption remain poorly constrained

steps.action: They take rival storage models from studies of other volcanoes: near- or sub-solidus cold storage with reheating, versus prolonged storage in an eruptible state.
steps.quote: Some favor storage at near-solidus temperature or even below solidus

steps.action: They cite the earlier estimates: one bulk garnet-glass-whole rock U-Th isochron for Mercato (Scheibner et al.), and much longer 1944 phenocryst residence times (Black et al.).
steps.quote: a single U-Th isochron date obtained from two multigrain garnet fractions

steps.action: They adopt the in situ LA-ICPMS U-Th garnet dating method developed in their own earlier work (Wotzlaw et al. 2019), with low-repetition-rate surface analyses.
steps.quote: we use recently developed techniques that allow in situ U-Th disequilibrium dating of Ca-rich garnet phenocrysts at the subcrystal scale

steps.action: They select the proximal pumice fall deposits of four past Plinian and sub-Plinian eruptions (Mercato, Avellino, Pompeii, Pollena), sampling white and gray pumices separately where the deposits are zoned (Methods p. 7).
steps.quote: unpolished garnet crystals from four major Plinian and sub-Plinian eruptions of Somma-Vesuvius

steps.action: They make 738 LA-ICPMS U-Th isotope analyses of garnet interiors and outermost rims.
steps.quote: We performed a total of 738 U-Th isotope analyses on both crystal interiors and [...]

steps.action: They fit internal U-Th isochrons in IsoplotR to obtain garnet crystallization ages and initial (230Th)/(232Th) for each eruption and pumice type.
steps.quote: U-Th isotope systematics of garnet phenocrysts yield well-defined internal isochrons

steps.action: They test whether low-U/Th apatite inclusions compromise the isochrons by recomputing isochrons from inclusion-free analyses only, which give indistinguishable but less precise dates.
steps.quote: This is consistent with isochrons obtained only from inclusionfree analyses, yielding indistinguishable but less precise dates.

steps.action: They check the U-Th measurement against secular-equilibrium garnet reference materials (Mali garnet; relative sensitivity factor 1.14 ± 0.08) and a monazite used for the abundance-sensitivity correction (Methods, fig. S6).
steps.quote: fig. S6 shows results for secular equilibrium garnets analyzed as reference materials

steps.action: They compare the in situ Mercato interior isochron date (14.56 ± 1.25 ka) with the independent bulk isochron of Scheibner et al. (14.4 ± 1.1 ka) and find agreement.
steps.quote: This is in excellent agreement with the bulk garnet-glass–whole rock isochron date of 14.4 ± 1.1 ka

steps.action: They measure garnet major and trace element compositions (EPMA, LA-ICPMS spots and line profiles), finding homogeneous Mercato garnets and reversely zoned Avellino, Pompeii and Pollena garnets.
steps.quote: garnets from the Avellino, Pompeii, and Pollena eruptions are compositionally zoned in major and trace elements

steps.action: They compute pre-eruption residence times as mean garnet age minus eruption age: about 5.7 ka for Mercato, about 4.9 to 5.0 ka for Avellino, about 0.9 to 1.4 ka for Pompeii and 0.8 ka for Pollena.
steps.quote: Mean pre-eruption residence times are here computed as the difference between the mean garnet crystallization age and the eruption age

steps.action: They reject recycling of garnets from earlier eruptions, because Pompeii and Pollena garnets differ in initial Th isotopic and trace element composition.
steps.quote: We did not find any evidence for recycling of garnets from previous eruptions.

steps.action: They compare residence times across the four eruptions with repose intervals, erupted volume and storage pressure: residence times decrease with age and scale with repose intervals, but not with volume or pressure.
steps.quote: they scale with the progressively shorter repose intervals

steps.action: They reject later garnet saturation as the cause of the shorter young residence times, using published phase equilibria.
steps.quote: Phase equilibria therefore do not explain the shorter garnet residence time in the Pompeii and Pollena magmas.

steps.action: They set garnet U-Th time scales against published crystal-size-distribution and Ba-diffusion time scales and argue the discrepancy reflects growth-rate uncertainty, larger crystals and rim-only recording, rather than cold storage.
steps.quote: Our estimates of upper crustal storage time scales based on garnet U-Th dates are significantly longer than residence time estimates based on sanidine

steps.action: From garnet zoning and garnet-glass trace element (dis)equilibrium, they infer reservoir assembly from progressively less evolved magma batches and different extents of recharge-related mixing in Avellino and Pompeii.
steps.quote: reservoirs were assembled from progressively less evolved magmas

steps.action: They keep the interpretation that resident upper-crustal phonolite, refilled rapidly after each eruption, blocked the ascent of mafic magma, and they draw the hazard implication that Plinian eruptions need centuries of quiescence.
steps.quote: the presence of phonolitic magma in the upper crust controlled the eruption dynamics of Somma-Vesuvius

steps.action: They compare garnet residence times with the 12 to 39 ka phenocryst residence times of the 1944 phonotephrites and infer a deeper, long-lived mafic reservoir.
steps.quote: The older crystal ages suggest the presence of a deeper-seated and long-lived mafic to intermediate reservoir

steps.action: They compute closed-system radioactive decay trajectories of initial (230Th)/(232Th) for (238U)/(232Th) of 1.2 and 2.0 and find the Mercato-to-Pompeii evolution consistent with decay.
steps.quote: is consistent with closed-system radioactive decay

steps.action: For the higher Pollena initial ratio, they weigh a distinct source magma against carbonate assimilation and favour assimilation, which is consistent with reservoir upward migration and published Sr isotope data.
steps.quote: assimilation of high U/Th crust such as shallow crustal carbonates

steps.action: They extend the Vesuvius composition versus residence time pattern to a global compilation of U-series major-phenocryst residence times and host compositions, finding a similar distribution (table S6, Fig. 5A).
steps.quote: We expanded a global compilation of U-series–derived crystal residence times (19)

steps.action: They compile zircon U-Th median residence times against host MgO for arc and intraplate volcanoes and compare them with the phenocryst data (table S7, Fig. 5B).
steps.quote: We further compiled zircon U-Th data and corresponding host magma compositions

steps.action: They keep the general claim of composition-dependent, distinct storage regimes: transient upper-crustal evolved chambers and long-lived deep mafic mushes.
steps.quote: points toward distinct magma storage regimes in crustal-scale magma plumbing systems

tree.answer: Duration and dynamics of pre-eruption phonolite storage beneath Somma-Vesuvius
No; inferred from garnet U-Th isochrons
Quantify residence times and reservoir evolution before four major eruptions
Cold vs warm storage (cited); garnet recycling; late garnet saturation; source vs assimilation for Pollena Th
Partly: recycling predicts shared initial Th and trace elements; phase equilibria predict saturation timing
Found: past eruption deposits known from traces

tree.question: 6b
tree.answer: Yes: four eruptions spanning ~9 ka give a residence time versus repose trend
Inclusion-free isochrons, reference garnets, agreement with independent Mercato date, global compilations
Kept: shortening residence times scaling with repose; phonolite controls eruption style

end.claim: Phonolite magmas resided in the upper crust for about 5.7 ka (Mercato), about 5 ka (Avellino) and about 1 ka or less (Pompeii, Pollena) before eruption, with residence times shortening through time and scaling with repose intervals.

decisive_move.sentence: In situ garnet U-Th isochron dating of interiors from four eruptions, converted to residence times, is the step without which neither the trend nor the eruption-dynamics interpretation would exist.

gates.evidence: Sampling was directed by the open question of storage duration (p. 1), not by a stated hypothesis. The residence-time trend could have failed to scale with repose. The recycling and late-saturation rivals were tested against initial Th, trace elements and phase equilibria (p. 4), but the eruption-dynamics interpretation is a best explanation with no failing test. Nothing is described as fixed before the data.

imports.item: Laser ablation inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (sector-field ICPMS) for in situ U-Th isotopes and trace elements
U-series radioactive decay and secular equilibrium used as chronometer and for reference-material calibration
NIST610/NIST612 reference glasses as primary and secondary standards
Two-dimensional kernel density estimate of the global compilation

limits: No review file was supplied; the acknowledgments mention two reviewers and editorial comments (p. 10), so any review-forced changes cannot be coded. Inference: there are no explicit 'first' statements, so novelty_claims is empty. Several key data sit in the supplement and were not seen: tables S5-S7, fig. S4 (trace elements across eruptions) and fig. S6 (reference garnets). Sub-claims have different statuses. The claim that phonolite presence controlled eruption dynamics and that Plinian eruptions need centuries of repose is a best_explanation (p. 5), not tested against a stated rival such as mafic supply rate. The global storage-regime claim is a regularity_in_range drawn from compiled data (pp. 5-7). Carbonate assimilation for Pollena is a best_explanation among two named options (p. 5). The trend rests on four eruptions; the two youngest dates overlap within uncertainty. The Pollena U-Th data were previously published (p. 2), so one of four data points is inherited. The paper does not report how many crystals were rejected or how isochron data points were screened beyond inclusion handling.

disagreements.target: Pappalardo and Mastrolorenzo (33), CSD-based residence times of 10^1 to 10^2 years
disagreements.support: Garnet U-Th residence times are much longer; the authors cite large growth-rate uncertainties and larger sanidine sizes (up to ~4 mm) in their Avellino sample.
disagreements.quote: Our estimates of upper crustal storage time scales based on garnet U-Th dates are significantly longer than residence time estimates based on sanidine

disagreements.target: Morgan et al. (11), Ba diffusion in sanidine giving ~10 years for AD 79
disagreements.support: The authors argue that Ba diffusion records only rim growth during pre-eruption recharge, while sanidine cores may be older.
disagreements.quote: Time scales based on Ba diffusion in sanidine only record the timing of high-Ba rim growth

disagreements.target: Cold storage and rapid remobilization interpretation of chronometer hiatus (Cooper and Kent, 19)
disagreements.support: The authors argue that the gap between U-series and CSD or diffusion time scales at Vesuvius is explained by method limitations, not low-temperature storage.
disagreements.quote: The hiatus between these chronometers has been interpreted to reflect intervals of magma storage at low temperature followed by rapid remobilization

disagreements.target: Pappalardo and Mastrolorenzo (33), polybaric supply system with short phonolite storage
disagreements.support: The authors agree with the polybaric architecture but find millennial, not decadal-centennial, phonolite storage times.
disagreements.quote: but they suggested substantially shorter phonolite storage and differentiation time scales

disagreements.target: Scaillet et al. (12), seismic attenuation zone at ~8 km as a growing phonolite body
disagreements.support: Because the current magma composition is unknown, the authors offer a tephritic supply system as an equally possible alternative.
disagreements.quote: this seismic attenuation zone may alternatively be part of the tephritic magma supply system

disagreements.target: Mastrolorenzo et al. (4), large Plinian eruption as worst-case scenario for future eruptions
disagreements.support: Residence times that scale with repose intervals imply that such eruptions require centuries of quiescence; the current repose is ~80 years.
disagreements.quote: often considered the worst-case scenario for future eruptions of Vesuvius (4), are therefore unlikely without several centuries of volcanic quiescence

alternatives_considered.chosen: Include analyses with small apatite inclusions in isochrons
alternatives_considered.reason: Inclusions are likely from boundary-layer crystallization and isochronous with host

alternatives_considered.chosen: Isochrons from crystal interiors; surface analyses plotted but excluded from isochron calculations
alternatives_considered.reason: Surface analyses have lower precision and often insufficient U/Th spread

alternatives_considered.chosen: Pollena garnets from various deposit portions analyzed as a single population
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Separate processing by portion (as done for Avellino and Pompeii white and gray pumices)

alternatives_considered.chosen: Garnet residence times record pre-eruption storage duration
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Recycling of garnets from previous eruptions; later garnet crystallization due to phase equilibria
alternatives_considered.reason: Distinct initial Th and trace element compositions; garnet stability ranges from experiments

alternatives_considered.chosen: Carbonate assimilation for higher Pollena initial (230Th)/(232Th)
alternatives_considered.alternatives: A distinct source magma with higher (238U)/(232Th)
alternatives_considered.reason: Coincides with upward reservoir migration into carbonate wall rock and with stable and radiogenic isotope evidence

alternatives_considered.chosen: Incorporation of zircon from source mush during melt extraction, for the most evolved magmas
alternatives_considered.alternatives: Zircon recording a longer crystallization interval; recycling of older zircons from earlier batches
alternatives_considered.reason: Crystal-poor rhyolites contain many near-eruption-age zircons and few older ones

alternatives_considered.alternatives: Bulk mineral separate U-Th data comprising hundreds of crystals
alternatives_considered.reason: Avoids averaging crystals with potentially different crystallization ages
